## Intercompany Netting Explained: Unlocking Efficiency, Simplifying Settlements, Reducing Risk


Intercompany netting solves a common treasury inefficiency: managing internal settlements across global subsidiaries.


Many multinational organizations process hundreds to thousands of intercompany invoices monthly across multiple currencies, legal entities, and banking relationships. Without a centralized approach, these internal payments can generate high banking fees, additional FX conversion costs, and manual reconciliation work that taxes treasury resources.


This mini guide covers how intercompany netting works, why it matters for treasury, and how to implement an effective automated intercompany netting program.


*This blog draws on insights from the webinar*[“Intercompany Netting: Unlocking Efficiency, Simplifying Settlements, Reducing Risk,”](https://www.corpay.com/resources/webcasts/intercompany-netting-unlocking-efficiency-simplifying-settlements-reducing) *featuring Jim Kessler, Vice President, Global Treasury Solutions, and Brandon Larsen, Vice President, Corporate Dealing.*


---


## What is Intercompany Netting?


Intercompany netting is a process used by multinational organizations to consolidate and offset internal payables and receivables between subsidiaries. Instead of every entity settling every invoice individually, transactions are aggregated and settled on a net basis, significantly reducing the number of payments required.


##### **Multilateral netting: the standard model for intercompany settlement**


For organizations with multiple subsidiaries, multilateral netting is the standard approach. Rather than netting between just two entities (bilateral netting), multilateral netting consolidates all intercompany transactions across every participating subsidiary. The system identifies offsets for receivables and payables enterprise-wide and calculates one net payment per currency.


---


## Why Intercompany Netting matters for treasury operations


As organizations grow globally, intercompany transaction volumes can increase dramatically. Without a centralized intercompany netting program, treasury teams often face:


Backlogs of intercompany invoices


High banking transfer costs


Increased FX conversion expenses and FX payment volumes


Fragmented visibility across entities


Significant time spent managing internal settlements


Intercompany netting addresses these challenges by centralizing the settlement process and bringing discipline to internal payment workflows.


---


## Key benefits of Intercompany Netting


Organizations implementing[intercompany netting](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/intercompany-netting-solutions-benefits) commonly experience improvements across several treasury functions.


-


**Reduced banking and FX conversion costs** Consolidating multiple transactions into a single net settlement can significantly reduce payment volumes, with industry examples showing reductions of approximately[70](https://www.pnc.com/insights/corporate-institutional/mitigate-risk/pharma-and-life-science-firms-simplify-cross-border-payments-with-fx-netting.html) -[90](https://ctmfile.com/sections/background/multi-lateral-netting) % in the number of intercompany transactions.


-


**Improved cash flow forecasting and liquidity management** Centralized settlement visibility enables treasury teams to better predict funding needs and manage liquidity positions more accurately. A structured netting cycle creates predictable cash movements, improving forecasting accuracy and strengthening global liquidity planning.


-


**Centralized control and operational efficiency** Standardized netting processes centralize payment data and reduce manual reconciliation, improving coordination across subsidiaries. Structured settlement cycles (monthly, quarterly, or semi-monthly) reduce ad-hoc funding activity, enhance operational discipline, and support more coordinated treasury decision-making.


-


**Enhanced governance and compliance** Intercompany netting strengthens governance through standardized settlement policies, approval workflows, audit trails, and role-based permissions, helping reduce operational risk across global treasury operations.


---


## Designing your Intercompany Netting program


While the concept is straightforward, several structural decisions shape how an intercompany netting program operates.


-


**Choosing payables vs. receivables netting** Many companies choose to base netting on payables, as it provides greater certainty that participating entities can fund required payments.


-


**Selecting a base currency** Netting settlements are typically tied to a base currency, often the headquarters currency, so funding requirements can be calculated consistently.


-


**Participation restrictions** Certain countries may require regulatory approval or may not allow participation in intercompany netting programs, which must be considered when designing the structure.


-


**Settlement frequency** Organizations may run netting cycles monthly, quarterly, or semi-monthly depending on transaction volumes and operational requirements.


-


**Choosing bilateral vs. multilateral netting** Organizations must decide whether to net balances between two entities (bilateral netting) or across multiple entities simultaneously (multilateral netting). While bilateral netting is simpler, multilateral netting is more efficient, reducing the number of settlements and improving overall liquidity management.


---


## How Intercompany Netting improves Treasury Visibility across the organization


Modern netting systems provide entity-level settlement views, allowing treasury teams to see net payable and receivable positions across subsidiaries in real time. This centralized visibility helps organizations identify intercompany FX exposures, track settlement obligations, and monitor funding requirements before settlement dates.


By adopting an automated netting solution integrated with FX trading capabilities, the company streamlined settlement workflows, improved transparency, reduced operational workload, and gained greater control over intercompany exposures.


---


## Automation: The foundation of effective netting programs


Automated intercompany netting platforms streamline the full process from invoice data capture and validation to settlement calculation, dispute management, and reporting.


Automated workflows reduce manual entry, improve accuracy, and ensure each settlement cycle runs consistently. Organizations typically upload invoice data, including selling entity, buying entity, currency, amount, transaction ID, and transaction date, from their ERP or accounting platform into a ‘netting center.’


Once uploaded, the system aggregates positions and calculates the net settlement for each participant.


##### **Example: The typical Intercompany Netting cycle**


1.


Data Capture: Entities submit intercompany invoice data for the settlement cycle.


2.


Analysis: Treasury reviews, validates, and locks the settlement period.


3.


Settlement Review: Net payable or receivable positions are calculated and reviewed.


4.


Dispute Management: Netting platforms allow disputed invoices to be flagged, excluded, or reviewed prior to settlement, ensuring only validated transactions are included in the cycle. Role-based permissions support governance by allowing different teams to review, approve, or manage disputes.


5.


Reporting: Final settlement results are published through dashboards and settlement reports, mapped to the company’s ERP.

## FAQs


**What is intercompany netting?**


Intercompany netting is a treasury process that consolidates and offsets payables and receivables between entities within the same organization. Instead of settling each intercompany invoice separately, subsidiaries settle their net positions, reducing the overall number of payments required.


**How does intercompany netting work?**


Intercompany netting aggregates transactions between participating entities during a defined settlement cycle. Payables and receivables are offset against one another, and each entity settles its remaining net payable or receivable position rather than processing every transaction individually.


**What are the benefits of intercompany netting?**


Intercompany netting can reduce banking fees, FX conversion costs, payment volumes, and manual reconciliation. It can also improve cash flow forecasting, liquidity management, treasury visibility, and control over intercompany settlements.


**What is the difference between bilateral and multilateral netting?**


Bilateral netting offsets transactions between two entities, while multilateral netting consolidates transactions across multiple entities. For multinational organizations with several subsidiaries, multilateral netting can significantly reduce the number of individual settlements required.


**How does intercompany netting reduce FX costs?**


By offsetting intercompany receivables and payables before settlement, companies can reduce the amount of currency that needs to be converted. This lowers FX transaction volumes and can reduce the associated conversion and cross-border payment costs.


**Can intercompany netting improve cash flow forecasting?**


Yes. Centralizing intercompany settlements gives treasury teams greater visibility into upcoming payable and receivable positions. Predictable settlement cycles can make it easier to forecast funding requirements and manage liquidity across the organization.


**Can intercompany netting be automated?**


Yes. Automated intercompany netting solutions can manage processes such as invoice data capture, validation, settlement calculations, dispute management, approvals, and reporting. Automation can reduce manual work while improving consistency and accuracy.


**How often should companies run an intercompany netting cycle?**


The appropriate frequency depends on transaction volumes and operational requirements. Organizations may run intercompany netting cycles monthly, semi-monthly, or quarterly based on their settlement needs.
